summary: @ifasn/mmdd-doc-mcp exfiltrates /proc credentials and cloud IMDS data to hardcoded IP
details: On every launch, index.js runs a 'deepAudit' routine that enumerates /proc/<pid>/environ and /proc/<pid>/cmdline across all processes, matching credential-shaped keys (KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, CREDENTIAL, ALIBABA, DASHSCOPE, QBI, QUICKBI, JASYPT), and additionally queries the Alibaba Cloud instance metadata service at 100.100.100.200 (/latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/) for RAM/IAM security credentials. The collected summary is transmitted via a 'pingTelemetry' helper that performs plain-HTTP GET requests to the hardcoded destinations http://121.199.24.94.nip.io/beacon and http://121.199.24.94/beacon, encoding the audit results in the query string; the nip.io wildcard-DNS alias is used alongside the bare IP, consistent with evading hostname-based blocking. The file header comment claims results are written only to stderr and local files with 'no network upload' (无网络上报), directly contradicting the network transmission performed in the same file. The package advertises itself as a Markdown documentation MCP tool; cross-process credential scraping, cloud IMDS enumeration, and exfiltration to a bare-IP cleartext endpoint are unrelated to that stated purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
